original_question: For a set of reals X, is the property S1(Gamma0,Gamma0) of Cp(X) equivalent to S1(Gamma,Gamma) of X?
target_in_paper: Problem 9.2 in §9, Function spaces and local-global principles: Is S1(Γ0,Γ0) for Cp(X) equivalent to S1(Γ,Γ) for X? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it asks about a set of reals X, the property S1(Γ0,Γ0) of Cp(X), and whether that is equivalent to S1(Γ,Γ) of X. That is exactly the official Problem 9.2 in §9. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
missing_details: The paper’s standing assumption in the remainder of §9 is that X is a subset of ℝ∖ℚ, not just an unspecified topological space. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
Cp(X) should be defined explicitly as the space of all continuous real-valued functions on X, endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
The point 0 must be identified as the constant zero function in Cp(X). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))

Γ0 needs to be unpacked via the local definition from §9: Γ0 is the family of countably infinite subsets A of Cp(X) such that 0 = lim A, i.e. 0 is not in A and every neighborhood of 0 contains all but finitely many elements of A. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
S1(A,B) should be stated explicitly: for each sequence (Un)n∈ℕ of members of A, one can choose Un∈Un for each n so that {Un:n∈ℕ} is a member of B. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))

Γ should be defined as the family of open γ-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite open cover U of X such that each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members of U; the paper also adopts the convention that a cover is nontrivial, meaning X itself is not an element of the cover. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))

To reflect the paper’s exact intent, it helps to note the known one-way implication stated immediately before the problem: S1(Γ,Γ) for X implies S1(Γ0,Γ0) for Cp(X), so the open issue is the converse. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
refined_question: Let X⊆ℝ∖ℚ, let Cp(X) be the space of all continuous real-valued functions on X with the topology of pointwise convergence, and let 0 denote the constant zero function. For collections A,B, write S1(A,B) to mean that for every sequence (Un)n∈ℕ of members of A, there exist Un∈Un for each n such that {Un:n∈ℕ} is a member of B. Let Γ0 be the family of countably infinite subsets A⊆Cp(X) with 0=lim A (equivalently, 0∉A and every neighborhood of 0 contains all but finitely many points of A), and let Γ be the family of open γ-covers of X, where a γ-cover is an infinite nontrivial open cover U of X such that each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. Since S1(Γ,Γ) for X is known to imply S1(Γ0,Γ0) for Cp(X), does the converse hold? Equivalently, is S1(Γ0,Γ0) for Cp(X) equivalent to S1(Γ,Γ) for X? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
equivalent_formulation: The paper states that S1(Γ0,Γ0) for Cp(X) is equivalent to S1(CΓ,CΓ) for X, where CΓ denotes the family of clopen γ-covers of X; therefore Problem 9.2 reduces to asking whether S1(Γ,Γ)=S1(CΓ,CΓ) for X. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
justification: The draft clearly targets §9 rather than any earlier problem: the wording is essentially the same as Problem 9.2. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the §1 definitions of S1 and γ-covers, the §9 local notation Γx at the point 0, the definition of Cp(X), and the hidden standing assumption X⊆ℝ∖ℚ. I also preserved the paper’s immediate contextual framing that one implication is already known and the open content is the converse. The alternate formulation is included only because the paper itself explicitly states the equivalence with S1(CΓ,CΓ). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609601))
